newsitem.title: USA: Forasol agrees to aquisition by Pride.
newsitem.headline: Forasol agrees to aquisition by Pride.

text.p: Forasol-Foramer N.V. said on Monday that it has agreed to be acquired by Pride Petroleum Services Inc.
The agreement provides that Forasol shareholders will receive 0.66 share of Pride common stock and $6.80 in cash for each share of Forasol commomn stock.
The firms said that the merger provides for break-up fees of up to $20 million. It is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 1997.
Pride Petroleum is a Houston, Texas-based provider of contract drilling and plugging and abandonment services.

Remi Dorval, Forasol's chief executive, will be appointed vice-chairman of Pride and Gerard Godde, Forasol's chief operating officer, will be appointed a senior vice-president of Pride and president and chief operating officer of Forasol.

In a statement, Dorval said, "This combination provides the size and financial resources to significantly expand Foramer's offshore fleet while also providing important synergies and growth opportunities in both our offshore and onshore operations."
Forasol said that pro forma for the combination, revenues of the combined company in 1997 are anticipated to be more than $750 million, with 30% attributed to offshore operations.
The combined company will also own in excess of 700 rigs, more than 40 of which are offshore rigs, and will conduct operations on and offshore in 20 countries worldwide.
